# The story

## A night in the life of a student {.center}

Last lecture, about 4 in 10 `bedtime` answers were still unreadable. Today we will finish the job, then ask what the *clean* times tell us:

1. When do students go to bed? (*Regular expressions*, Chapter 15)
2. When do they wake up, and who is still awake at 1 AM? (*Dates and times*, Chapter 17)


<!-- r setup -->
```{r echo=FALSE}
#| context: setup
library(dplyr)
library(tibble)
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyverse)
library(readr)

survey <- read_csv("data/sleep_survey_v2.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
survey_clean <- survey |>
  mutate(
    clean = str_to_lower(str_trim(bedtime)),
    clean = str_remove(clean, "^(around|about|~) ?"),
    clean = str_remove(clean, "-ish$"),
    clean = str_replace(clean, "midnight", "12:00 am"),
    clean = str_replace(clean, "a\\.m\\.", "am"),
    clean = str_replace(clean, "p\\.m\\.", "pm"),
    clean = str_replace(clean, "\\.", ":")
  ) |>
  separate_wider_regex(
    clean,
    patterns = c(hh = "\\d{1,2}", ":?", mm = "\\d{0,2}", " ?", ampm = "am|pm|"),
    too_few = "align_start"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    hh = as.numeric(hh),
    mm = if_else(mm == "", 0, as.numeric(mm)),
    hour24 = case_when(
      ampm == "am" ~ hh %% 12,
      ampm == "pm" ~ hh %% 12 + 12,
      hh >= 13 | hh == 0 ~ hh,
      hh >= 6 & hh <= 11 ~ hh + 12,
      hh <= 5 | hh == 12 ~ hh %% 12
    )
  )
sleep_times <- survey_clean |>
  filter(!is.na(hour24), !is.na(sleep_hours)) |>
  mutate(
    bedtime_dt = make_datetime(2026, 10, 27, tz = "America/Toronto") +
      hours(if_else(hour24 < 12, hour24 + 24, hour24)) +
      minutes(mm),
    wake = bedtime_dt + dhours(sleep_hours),
    wake_clock = hour(wake) + minute(wake) / 60
  )
asleep <- sleep_times |>
  mutate(
    sleeping = interval(bedtime_dt, wake),
    asleep_1am = make_datetime(2026, 10, 28, 1, tz = "America/Toronto") %within% sleeping
  )
```

# Part 1: Regular expressions


## When do students go to bed? {.smaller}

Our goal: turn every typed `bedtime` into an hour and a minute on a 24-hour clock.

| Step | Tool (Chapter 15) |
|------|-------------------|
| Test for a pattern | `str_detect()`, `regex(ignore_case = TRUE)` |
| Describe a pattern | `\\d`, `[:.]`, `?`, `{1,2}`, `^`, `$`, `(am\|pm)` |
| Tidy the text | `str_replace()`, `str_remove()` |
| Pull the pieces out | `separate_wider_regex()` |
| Decide the rules | `case_when()` (Lecture 8) |

## Does it match? 

:::{.callout-note title="`str_detect(x, pattern)`"}
This function returns a logical vector. It takes a look at `x` and asks for the `pattern`. It returns a `TRUE` where the pattern is found.
:::

```{webr}
x <- c("11:30 pm", "23:30", "midnight", "idk")
str_detect(x, "pm")
str_detect(x, "\\d") # "\\d" means digits (from 0 to 9)
```

On the survey:

```{webr}
survey |>
  count(has_pm = str_detect(bedtime, "pm"))
```


## Capital letters matter

`"PM"` and `"pm"` are different to a regular expression. Wrap the pattern in `regex()` to ignore the case:

```{webr}
survey |> count(exact_case = str_detect(bedtime, "pm"))
survey |> count(any_case = str_detect(bedtime, regex("pm", ignore_case = TRUE)))
```

- The second count finds more `TRUE`s: it also catches `PM` and `Pm`

## Building blocks of a pattern {.smaller}

| Pattern | Matches |
|---------|---------|
| `.` | any **one** character |
| `\\.` | a real dot |
| `\\d` | one digit |
| `[:.]` | a colon **or** a dot |
| `?` | the piece before it is optional (0 or 1 times) |
| `{1,2}` | the piece before it appears 1 or 2 times |
| `^` and `$` | the start and the end of the string |
| <code>(am&#124;pm)</code> | `am` **or** `pm` |

::: {.callout-warning title="Two backslashes in R"}
In an R string, a backslash must be **escaped**. To get the regex `\d`, you type `"\\d"`. To match a real dot, you type `"\\."`, because a plain `.` matches anything.
:::

## A pattern for the standard format

`"11:30 pm"` is: one or two digits, a colon, two digits, an optional space, then `am` or `pm`.

```{webr}
pattern <- "^\\d{1,2}:\\d{2} ?(am|pm)$"

x <- c("11:30 pm", "11:30PM", "1:05 am", "23:30", "11.30 pm")
str_detect(x, regex(pattern, ignore_case = TRUE))
```

- `^` and `$` force the pattern to match the **whole** string
- Without them, `"around 11:30 pm"` would also match

## How many bedtimes match?

```{webr}
pattern <- "^\\d{1,2}:\\d{2} ?(am|pm)$"

survey |>
  count(standard = str_detect(bedtime, regex(pattern, ignore_case = TRUE)))
```

## What is left?

The trick with regular expressions: look at what does **not** match, and improve the pattern.

```{webr}
survey |>
  filter(!str_detect(bedtime, regex("^\\d{1,2}:\\d{2} ?(am|pm)$", ignore_case = TRUE))) |>
  count(bedtime, sort = TRUE)
```


## Cleaning

- `str_replace(x, pattern, replacement)` replaces the **first** match
- `str_remove(x, pattern)` deletes it
- `str_replace_all()` replaces **every** match (see the appendix)

```{webr}
x <- c(" Around 11:30PM", "~12:30am-ish", "11.30 p.m.", "midnight")

x |>
  str_trim() |>
  str_to_lower() |>
  str_remove("^(around|about|~) ?") |>
  str_remove("-ish$") |>
  str_replace("midnight", "12:00 am") |>
  str_replace("p\\.m\\.", "pm") |>
  str_replace("\\.", ":")
```

## Apply the rules to the survey

```{webr}
survey |>
  mutate(
    clean = str_to_lower(str_trim(bedtime)),
    clean = str_remove(clean, "^(around|about|~) ?"),
    clean = str_remove(clean, "-ish$"),
    clean = str_replace(clean, "midnight", "12:00 am"),
    clean = str_replace(clean, "a\\.m\\.", "am"),
    clean = str_replace(clean, "p\\.m\\.", "pm"),
    clean = str_replace(clean, "\\.", ":")
  ) |>
  count(standard = str_detect(clean, "^\\d{1,2}(:\\d{2})? ?(am|pm)$"))
```

- Many more rows match, and we did not touch the data by hand
- The rest are 24-hour times, times with no `am` or `pm`, and answers like `idk`

## Pulling the pieces out

::: {.callout-note title="`separate_wider_regex()`"}
Last lecture we split on a space. A regular expression can split on a *pattern*. Each named piece becomes a column; unnamed pieces are matched and dropped.
:::

```{webr}
df <- tibble(clean = c("11:30 pm", "2330", "11 pm", "12:00 am", "idk"))

df |>
  separate_wider_regex(
    clean,
    patterns = c(
      hh = "\\d{1,2}",
      ":?",
      mm = "\\d{0,2}",
      " ?",
      ampm = "am|pm|"
    ),
    too_few = "align_start"
  )
```

::: {.callout-tip title="Optional pieces"}
`\\d{0,2}` allows **no** minutes, and the empty option at the end of `am|pm|` allows **no** `am` or `pm`. Strings that do not fit at all, like `idk`, become `NA`.
:::

## Deciding the rules

::: {.callout-tip title="We need rules!"}
Some answers have no `am` or `pm`: `23:30`, `0100`, or just `11:30`. If it is

- Already 24-hour (13 to 23, or 0): keep the hour
- 6 to 11 with no `am` or `pm`: assume **evening** (add 12)
- 12 or 1 to 5 with no `am` or `pm`: assume **after midnight**
:::

```{webr}
df <- tibble(hh = c(11, 11, 23, 1, 12), ampm = c("pm", "", "", "", ""))

df |>
  mutate(
    hour24 = case_when(
      ampm == "am" ~ hh %% 12,
      ampm == "pm" ~ hh %% 12 + 12,
      hh >= 13 | hh == 0 ~ hh,
      hh >= 6 & hh <= 11 ~ hh + 12,
      hh <= 5 | hh == 12 ~ hh %% 12
    )
  )
```

::: {.callout-important title="Order matters"}
`case_when()` uses the first match, as we talked about this with *Logical Vectors*. The 24-hour rule comes before the "6 to 11" rule for a reason.
:::

## Putting Part 1 together


```{webr}
#| autorun: TRUE
survey_clean <- survey |>
  mutate(
    clean = str_to_lower(str_trim(bedtime)),
    clean = str_remove(clean, "^(around|about|~) ?"),
    clean = str_remove(clean, "-ish$"),
    clean = str_replace(clean, "midnight", "12:00 am"),
    clean = str_replace(clean, "a\\.m\\.", "am"),
    clean = str_replace(clean, "p\\.m\\.", "pm"),
    clean = str_replace(clean, "\\.", ":")
  ) |>
  separate_wider_regex(
    clean,
    patterns = c(hh = "\\d{1,2}", ":?", mm = "\\d{0,2}", " ?", ampm = "am|pm|"),
    too_few = "align_start"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    hh = as.numeric(hh),
    mm = if_else(mm == "", 0, as.numeric(mm)),
    hour24 = case_when(
      ampm == "am" ~ hh %% 12,
      ampm == "pm" ~ hh %% 12 + 12,
      hh >= 13 | hh == 0 ~ hh,
      hh >= 6 & hh <= 11 ~ hh + 12,
      hh <= 5 | hh == 12 ~ hh %% 12
    )
  )

survey_clean |>
  summarize(
    readable = sum(!is.na(hour24)),
    blank = sum(is.na(bedtime)),
    unreadable = sum(is.na(hour24) & !is.na(bedtime))
  )
```


## The answer so far

```{webr}
survey_clean |>
  filter(!is.na(hour24)) |>
  mutate(
    bed_hour = hour24 + mm / 60,
    bed_hour = if_else(bed_hour < 12, bed_hour + 24, bed_hour)
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = bed_hour)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.5, boundary = 0, closed = "left") +
  facet_wrap(~ program) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = c(21, 24, 27),
    labels = c("9 PM", "12 AM", "3 AM")
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Bedtimes by program",
    x = "Bedtime", y = "Students"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14)
```

- This is last lecture's plot, with half-hour bins and **many more** students
- Engineering goes to bed later than Arts

::: {.callout-note title="What is still missing?"}
Blank answers and answers like `idk` are still `NA`. We cannot recover what students did not tell us.
:::

# Part 2: Dates and times



## When do they wake up?

Wake-up time is **bedtime plus sleep**. To add them we need real date-times, just not text!

| Step | Tool (Chapter 17) |
|------|-------------------|
| Create date-times | `ymd()`, `ymd_hms()`, `make_datetime()` |
| Get the pieces | `hour()`, `minute()`, `wday()` |
| Add time | `hours()`, `dhours()` |
| Test for overlap | `interval()`, `%within%` |
| Fix the time zone | `force_tz()`, `with_tz()` |

## Creating date-times from text

The function name spells the **order** of the pieces:

```{webr}
ymd("2026-10-27")
mdy("October 27, 2026")
dmy("27-Oct-2026")
ymd_hms("2026-10-27 14:32:05")
```

::: {.callout-tip title="Any separator works"}
`ymd()` ignores dashes, slashes, and spaces. Only the order of year, month and day matters.
:::

## Creating date-times from parts

::: {.callout-note title="`make_datetime()`"}
This function builds a date-time from separate numbers. Adding *periods* such as `hours()` moves the clock forward.
:::

```{webr}
make_datetime(2026, 10, 27, 23, 30)

# 25 hours after midnight on Oct 27 is 1 AM on Oct 28
make_datetime(2026, 10, 27) + hours(25) + minutes(30)
```

- This is how we handle bedtimes *after midnight*: add 24 hours, and the date rolls over

## Bedtime as a date-time

We pick one reference night (e.g. *October 27, 2026*), and add the hour and minute:

```{webr}
survey_clean |>
  filter(!is.na(hour24)) |>
  mutate(
    bedtime_dt = make_datetime(2026, 10, 27, tz = "America/Toronto") +
      hours(if_else(hour24 < 12, hour24 + 24, hour24)) +
      minutes(mm)
  ) |>
  select(student_id, bedtime, bedtime_dt)
```

- Use `if_else()` to add 24 to the after-midnight hours
- `tz = "America/Toronto"` is the time zone. More on that soon

## Getting the pieces back

```{webr}
t <- ymd_hms("2026-10-27 06:35:00")

hour(t)
minute(t)
wday(t, label = TRUE)
month(t)
```

:::{.callout-warning title="Checkpoint"}
What is the difference between `wday(t)` and `day(t)`?
:::

## Time spans

::: {.callout-tip title="Two way to add time"}
- **Durations** (`dhours()`, `ddays()`) are an exact number of seconds
- **Periods** (`hours()`, `days()`) move the **clock** by a calendar amount
:::

::: {.callout-caution title="When to use it?"}
- Use *durations* for how long something lasts, like sleep. 
- Use *periods* for calendar time.
:::


## Daylight Savings

Toronto switches to daylight saving time on November 1, 2026 starting at midnight.

```{webr}
start <- ymd_hms("2026-11-01 00:00:00", tz = "America/Toronto")

start + days(1)
start + ddays(1)
```

::: {.callout-important title="Which one should I use?"}
`days(1)` gives midnight on November 2 where the clock moved one day. `ddays(1)` gives *11 PM*: exactly 24 hours later, but the clocks jumped back in 1 hour. 
:::

## Duration

::: {.callout-important title="Quick Maths"}
`Wake-up time = bedtime + sleep`. Sleep is a duration, so we use `dhours()`.
:::

```{webr}
#| autorun: TRUE
sleep_times <- survey_clean |>
  filter(!is.na(hour24), !is.na(sleep_hours)) |>
  mutate(
    bedtime_dt = make_datetime(2026, 10, 27, tz = "America/Toronto") +
      hours(if_else(hour24 < 12, hour24 + 24, hour24)) +
      minutes(mm),
    wake = bedtime_dt + dhours(sleep_hours),
    wake_clock = hour(wake) + minute(wake) / 60
  )

sleep_times |>
  select(student_id, bedtime_dt, sleep_hours, wake)
```


## Do students with an early class wake up earlier?

```{webr}
sleep_times |>
  mutate(early = if_else(has_early_class == "Yes", "Has an early class", "No early class")) |>
  filter(!is.na(early)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = wake_clock)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.5, boundary = 0, closed = "left") +
  facet_wrap(~ early, ncol = 1) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = 4:10,
    labels = c("4 AM", "5 AM", "6 AM", "7 AM", "8 AM", "9 AM", "10 AM")
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Students with an early class wake up earlier",
    x = "Wake-up time", y = "Students"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14)
```


## Average wake-up time


```{webr}
sleep_times |>
  filter(!is.na(has_early_class)) |>
  group_by(has_early_class) |>
  summarize(mean_wake = mean(wake_clock)) |>
  mutate(
    hours = mean_wake %/% 1,
    minutes = round((mean_wake %% 1) * 60)
  )
```

## Who is asleep at 1 AM?

:::{.callout-note title="Interval"}
The stretch of time between two date-times. `x %within% interval` is `TRUE` when `x` falls inside the interval.
:::

```{webr}
asleep <- sleep_times |>
  mutate(
    sleeping = interval(bedtime_dt, wake),
    asleep_1am = make_datetime(2026, 10, 28, 1, tz = "America/Toronto") %within% sleeping
  )

asleep |>
  count(asleep_1am)
```


## Who is asleep at 1 AM?

```{r echo=FALSE}
asleep |>
  group_by(program) |>
  summarize(share_asleep = mean(asleep_1am)) |>
  mutate(program = fct_reorder(program, share_asleep)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = share_asleep, y = program)) +
  geom_col() +
  geom_text(aes(label = scales::percent(share_asleep, accuracy = 1)), hjust = -0.1) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.2))) +
  labs(
    title = "Share of students asleep at 1 AM",
    x = NULL, y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14)
```

## Code

```{r echo=FALSE}
asleep |>
  group_by(program) |>
  summarize(share_asleep = mean(asleep_1am)) |>
  mutate(program = fct_reorder(program, share_asleep)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = share_asleep, y = program)) +
  geom_col() +
  geom_text(aes(label = scales::percent(share_asleep, accuracy = 1)), hjust = -0.1) +

```


## Better sleep = better grades?

```{r echo=FALSE}
sleep_times |>
  mutate(
    after_midnight = bedtime_dt > make_datetime(2026, 10, 6, tz = "America/Toronto")
  ) |>
  filter(!is.na(avg_grade)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = sleep_hours, y = avg_grade, colour = after_midnight)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
  scale_colour_manual(
    values = c("FALSE" = "grey60", "TRUE" = "firebrick"),
    labels = c("Bed before midnight", "Awake after midnight"),
    name = NULL
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Sleep and grades, by bedtime",
    x = "Hours of sleep", y = "Average grade"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14)
```

## Code

```{r eval=FALSE}
sleep_times |>
  mutate(
    after_midnight = bedtime_dt > make_datetime(2026, 10, 6, tz = "America/Toronto")
  ) |>
  filter(!is.na(avg_grade)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = sleep_hours, y = avg_grade, colour = after_midnight)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
  scale_colour_manual(
    values = c("FALSE" = "grey60", "TRUE" = "firebrick"),
    labels = c("Bed before midnight", "Awake after midnight"),
    name = NULL
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Sleep and grades, by bedtime",
    x = "Hours of sleep", y = "Average grade"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14)
```

## What does the scatter plot say?

::: {.callout-caution title="What is after midnight?"}
We used `>`, so a student at exactly 12:00 AM counts as **before** midnight. Change it to `>=` and see what happens. Boundaries matter, as with `cut()` last lecture.
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Observations"}
The red points sit to the left: students who go to bed after midnight sleep less. They also have slightly lower grades, but the two clouds overlap a lot.
:::

## Exercise 2

::: {.callout-tip title="Live exercise"}
Suppose that I have given you a tiny data set of three students. Their bedtime is a date-time, and sleep is in hours.

1. Compute each student's wake-up time.
2. Is each student asleep at 3:00 AM on October 28?
3. What share of the three students is asleep at 3:00 AM?
:::

```{webr}
#| exercise: ex_dates
df <- tibble(
  student = c("A", "B", "C"),
  bedtime = ymd_hms(
    c("2026-10-27 23:30:00", "2026-10-28 00:45:00", "2026-10-28 03:15:00"),
    tz = "America/Toronto"
  ),
  sleep_hours = c(7.5, 6, 4.25)
)

df |>
  mutate(
    wake = ,
    asleep_3am =
  )
```

```{webr}
#| exercise: ex_dates
#| solution: true
df <- tibble(
  student = c("A", "B", "C"),
  bedtime = ymd_hms(
    c("2026-10-27 23:30:00", "2026-10-28 00:45:00", "2026-10-28 03:15:00"),
    tz = "America/Toronto"
  ),
  sleep_hours = c(7.5, 6, 4.25)
)

df2 <- df |>
  mutate(
    wake = bedtime + dhours(sleep_hours),
    asleep_3am = make_datetime(2026, 10, 28, 3, tz = "America/Toronto") %within%
      interval(bedtime, wake)
  )

df2

# Student C goes to bed at 3:15, after 3:00, so only 2 of 3 are asleep
df2 |>
  summarize(share_asleep = mean(asleep_3am))
```

# Appendix: read the text

## Regular expressions: other tools (i) {.smaller}

| Tool | What it does | Tiny example | Read the section on |
|------|--------------|--------------|---------------------|
| `str_count()` | Counts how many times a pattern appears in each string | `str_count("banana", "a")` | Counting matches |
| `str_extract()` | Pulls out the matching text itself | `str_extract("11:30 pm", "\\d+")` | Extracting |
| `str_replace_all()` | Replaces **every** match, not just the first | `str_replace_all("a.b.c", "\\.", "-")` | Replacing values |


## Regular expressions: other tools (ii) {.smaller}

| Tool | What it does | Tiny example | Read the section on |
|------|--------------|--------------|---------------------|
| `str_view()` | Shows where a pattern matches, highlighted | `str_view(x, "pm")` | Pattern basics |
| Back references: `\\1` | Reuses the text a group captured | `str_replace(x, "(\\d+)h", "\\1 hours")` | Grouping and capturing |
| `fixed()` | Matches the exact text, with no special characters | `str_detect(x, fixed("."))` | Fixed matches |

## Regular expressions: other tools (iii) {.smaller}

| Tool | What it does | Tiny example | Read the section on |
|------|--------------|--------------|---------------------|
| `regex()` flags | `multiline`, `comments`, and more | `regex("pm", ignore_case = TRUE)` | Pattern control |
| `+`, `*` | One or more, zero or more | `"\\d+"` | Quantifiers |
| `[^...]` | Anything **except** these characters | `"[^0-9]"` | Character classes |


## Regular expressions: other tools (iv) {.smaller}

| Tool | What it does | Tiny example | Read the section on |
|------|--------------|--------------|---------------------|
| `\\s`, `\\w` | A space; a letter, digit or underscore | `"\\s+"` | Character classes |
| Parentheses | Control the order of `\|` and quantifiers | `"(am&#124;pm)$"` | Operator precedence |


## Dates and times: other tools (i) {.smaller}

| Tool | What it does | Tiny example | Read the section on |
|------|--------------|--------------|---------------------|
| `make_date()` | Builds a date from year, month and day | `make_date(2026, 10, 6)` | Creating date-times |
| `as_datetime()`, `as_date()` | Converts between a date and a date-time | `as_date(now())` | Creating date-times |
| `yday()`, `mday()` | Day of the year, day of the month | `yday(ymd("2026-10-06"))` | Getting components |
| `round_date()`, `ceiling_date()` | Round to the nearest unit, or up | `ceiling_date(x, "hour")` | Rounding |


## Dates and times: other tools (ii) {.smaller}

| Tool | What it does | Tiny example | Read the section on |
|------|--------------|--------------|---------------------|
| `update()` | Changes one component of a date-time | `update(x, hour = 6)` | Modifying components |
| `as.duration()` | Turns a time difference into a duration | `as.duration(end - start)` | Durations |
| `%--%` | A shortcut for `interval()` | `start %--% end` | Intervals |



## Dates and times: other tools (iii) {.smaller}

| Tool | What it does | Tiny example | Read the section on |
|------|--------------|--------------|---------------------|
| `int_length()` | The length of an interval in seconds | `int_length(sleeping)` | Intervals |
| `Sys.timezone()` | Your computer's time zone | `Sys.timezone()` | Time zones |

::: {.callout-tip title="Everything has a time zone"}
Date-times without an explicit time zone are treated as **UTC**. Always check with `tz()` before you compute hours.
:::
